blocks.title: Current answers, with the sources still attached
blocks.description: Web Access gives the agent two abilities: search the public web, and read a page or PDF down to the paragraph. It works the moment you install it — the free default needs no key — and you can point it at your own provider or private SearXNG instance when you want your own quota or index.

showcase.user_prompt: Compare the current pricing of these three note-taking apps from their official pages.
showcase.assistant_reply: I searched for each product's pricing page, then read all three. Two publish a monthly price; the third only lists an annual plan, so I am quoting it per year instead of converting it. Sources: app-one.com/pricing, app-two.com/plans, app-three.com/billing — the numbers are from today's pages, not from a cached snippet.

items.title: Search without setup
items.description: The free Exa endpoint answers immediately, so a fresh install can already look things up. No account, no key.

items.title: Read the page, not just the snippet
items.description: web_fetch turns an article, docs page or PDF into clean Markdown, with the character budget you set.

items.title: Bring your own provider
items.description: Add an Exa, Brave, Tavily or Bocha key, or point the plugin at a SearXNG instance you run yourself.

items.title: Automatic fallback
items.description: Configured providers are tried first; an empty result or a rejected key falls through to the free one instead of ending the turn.

items.title: Private by default, with a switch
items.description: localhost and LAN addresses are blocked, and hosted readers are opt-out. When a page cannot be read directly, the plugin tells you which reader saw the URL.

items.title: One page to test it
items.description: Settings → More options → Web Access runs a real query with the values on screen, so a bad key shows its own error before you rely on it.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: Search and page reading work with the free default. Nothing to register.

items.title: Ask, or hand it a URL
items.description: “What changed in the latest release?” makes the agent search. “Read this page and give me the numbers, with sources” makes it fetch the page you pasted.

items.title: Add a key only if you want one
items.description: Open Settings → More options → Web Access to add a provider key, switch to SearXNG, turn off hosted readers, or allow local addresses.

blocks.content: The free default search sends your query to Exa. Reading a page normally goes straight from your machine; if the page is JavaScript-heavy, blocks bots, or is a PDF, the URL is sent to Exa's reader (and to Jina when you configured it) unless you turn the fallback off. Page content, keys and settings stay on this machine.
